lastCompletedStory.title: CRITICAL: Even when the viewer pane survives, it freezes permanently at the first rotate.

openQuestions: CAM-513 (flaky-test-isolation, filed on main from US-R1-003) remains open and unrelated to this story's diff.

US-R2-004 (WARNING: every existing test in test/setup-config-log.test.ts spawns snippets under an explicit bash, never the real /bin/sh production tmux hands pipe-pane -o commands to) is still open; this story's new tests also run buildConfigLogCapCommand under bash/spawn('tail', ...), not the real /bin/sh, so they do not close that gap either.
US-R2-005 (site 4 has no stale-sibling pruning, unlike sites 1/2/3/5) remains open and untouched by this story.
nextStoryContext: US-R2-003 fixed the reviewer's CRITICAL finding that the v|V read-only viewer pane freezes permanently at the first log rotate. buildConfigLogCapCommand's rotate step wrote the trimmed tail back via `tail -c N LOG > LOG.tmp && mv LOG.tmp LOG`; `mv` unlinks LOG's directory entry and repoints it at LOG.tmp's freshly-created inode, but the viewer pane's `tail -f $CAM_CONFIG_LOG` had already opened LOG by descriptor and, per GNU coreutils' own manual (confirmed via Step 5.5 WebFetch), `--follow=descriptor` (tail -f's default) explicitly does NOT detect that the file has been unlinked or renamed -- it keeps following the original, now-detached inode forever, so the viewer stops receiving any bytes written after the very first rotate and never recovers. Reviewer repro under real tmux with a pre-created log and a 3000-byte ceiling: viewer frozen on MARK-89 at t+3s and still MARK-89 at t+11s while the log itself had advanced past MARK-462. US-R1-004 (every-4KB-ish rotate cadence, actually every CONFIG_LOG_CEILING_BYTES=200000 bytes) converted this from a once-per-session cosmetic detail into a freeze within the first few hundred KB of output. Fix: rotate in place instead of switching the viewer to tail -F/--follow=name -- the rotate line now does `tail -c N LOG > LOG.tmp && cat LOG.tmp > LOG && rm -f LOG.tmp`; `cat X > Y` (shell output redirection) opens Y's EXISTING inode and truncates it in place rather than creating a new one, so the inode the viewer's tail -f already has open by descriptor never changes across a rotate. The same GNU manual confirms --follow=descriptor explicitly detects in-place truncation and resumes tracking from the new (shorter) content, so no follow-mode flag change was needed. Chose rotate-in-place over -F specifically because this codebase already treats /bin/sh and coreutils variance across the macOS-vs-Linux shipped binaries as a real portability axis (the US-R2-001 dash-arithmetic bullet in patterns.md), and rotating in place sidesteps needing any follow-mode flag's exact semantics to hold across both platforms. Doc comment on buildConfigLogCapCommand (src/commands/setup.ts) now explains the mv-vs-cat-in-place inode distinction and the reviewer's exact MARK-89/MARK-462 repro. Three new tests added to test/setup-config-log.test.ts's buildConfigLogCapCommand describe block: (1) a structural guard asserting the generated snippet never contains a bare `mv` word and does contain `cat`; (2) an inode-preservation test that stat()s the pre-created log file's `.ino` before feeding input past the ceiling under real bash, then asserts the post-rotate `.ino` is identical; (3) an end-to-end live-tail-f regression that spawns a real `tail -f` process against the pre-created log BEFORE the writer starts, feeds 200 MARK-N lines through the real buildConfigLogCapCommand snippet (forcing several real rotates at a 500-byte ceiling), and asserts the tail -f process's captured stdout eventually contains MARK-199 -- directly falsifying the freeze this story closes, since a pre-fix (mv-based) rotate would have left tail -f's captured output stuck at whatever mark was current right before the first rotate. Full bun test 6104 pass / 0 fail (+3 from the new tests, unchanged failure count), typecheck 0 errors, full bun run check:all spine green after two justified gate resolutions: (a) file-size-budget.json raised for src/commands/setup.ts (1059->1076, the expanded doc comment plus the 3 new lines in the rotate command and the new test bodies), dated note prepended to _ref naming this story/CAM-510 and staged in the same commit; (b) knip.json's ignoreBinaries list gained "tail" (the new live-tail-f regression test spawns the real `tail` binary directly via node:child_process, alongside the pre-existing ps/lsof/pgrep/tmux/gh entries in the same allowlist, all real POSIX/tmux utilities the test suite legitimately shells out to). No vendor/templates changes, no embed-vendor needed. Step 5.5 fetched the current GNU coreutils tail manual (confirming both halves of the mechanism: --follow=descriptor does not detect rename/unlink, and DOES detect in-place truncation and resumes tracking) -- aligned with and fully explains the reviewer's real-tmux repro, no correction needed to the implementation. scripts/cam/prd.json was left untouched/uncommitted by this story, per the AGENT.md rule that the implementer never edits prd.json.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed tail -f's default --follow=descriptor mode does NOT detect that a followed file has been renamed/unlinked (it keeps reading the original, now-detached inode forever, which is exactly the CAM-510 US-R2-003 freeze mechanism when the rotate used mv), but DOES detect in-place truncation on the SAME inode and resumes tracking from the new content -- confirming rotate-in-place (cat TMP > LOG) as the correct closure, no --follow=name/-F flag change needed.
